sentences.en: What is the weather like today?
It is sunny but a little windy.
The temperature is rising.
It might rain this evening.
Did you check the forecast?
There is a chance of thunderstorms.
Take an umbrella just in case.
The sky is getting cloudy.
I can hear thunder in the distance.
It started raining suddenly.
The roads are wet and slippery.
It feels colder than yesterday.
sentences.ar: الجو أبرد مما كان عليه أمس.

sentences.en: I need a warmer jacket.
Winter evenings can be chilly.
Summer days are very hot here.
I prefer mild weather.
Spring is my favorite season.
The flowers bloom in spring.
Autumn brings cooler mornings.
The air feels fresh after the rain.
It is too humid to go running.
Remember to drink enough water.
sentences.ar: تذكر أن تشرب كمية كافية من الماء.

sentences.en: The sun sets later in summer.
sentences.ar: تغرب الشمس في وقت متأخر صيفًا.

sentences.en: We should avoid the midday heat.
There is a strong wind outside.
The dust makes it hard to see.
I will close the windows.
The weather is improving now.
Let us enjoy the cool breeze.
The forecast says tomorrow will be clear.
sentences.ar: تقول التوقعات إن الغد سيكون صحوًا.

sentences.en: We can have a picnic this weekend.
sentences.ar: يمكننا الخروج في نزهة نهاية الأسبوع.

sentences.en: I hope the rain stops soon.
Every season has something special.
Good weather makes the day brighter.

sections.heading: A new situation
paragraphs: Dina was learning how to handle weather and seasons in everyday English. The goal was to communicate clearly and politely. Dina practiced “What is the weather like today?” A useful phrase was “It is sunny but a little windy.” A useful phrase was “The temperature is rising.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “It might rain this evening.” A useful phrase was “Did you check the forecast?” A useful phrase was “There is a chance of thunderstorms.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Take an umbrella just in case.” A useful phrase was “The sky is getting cloudy.” A useful phrase was “I can hear thunder in the distance.” They repeated it to remember the meaning.

sections.heading: Finding the right words
paragraphs: As the situation developed, Dina listened carefully and tried more useful expressions. Dina practiced “It started raining suddenly.” A useful phrase was “The roads are wet and slippery.” A useful phrase was “It feels colder than yesterday.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. sections.heading: Making a choice
paragraphs: There were more details to understand, so Dina slowed down and chose the next words thoughtfully. Dina practiced “Autumn brings cooler mornings.” A useful phrase was “The air feels fresh after the rain.” A useful phrase was “It is too humid to go running.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Remember to drink enough water.” A useful phrase was “The sun sets later in summer.” A useful phrase was “We should avoid the midday heat.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “There is a strong wind outside.” A useful phrase was “The dust makes it hard to see.”

sections.heading: A confident finish
paragraphs: At the end of the activity, Dina reviewed the final expressions and felt more comfortable speaking. Dina practiced “I will close the windows.” A useful phrase was “The weather is improving now.” A useful phrase was “Let us enjoy the cool breeze.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “The forecast says tomorrow will be clear.” A useful phrase was “We can have a picnic this weekend.” A useful phrase was “I hope the rain stops soon.” They repeated it to remember the meaning. Dina practiced “Every season has something special.” A useful phrase was “Good weather makes the day brighter.”
